text:
anya: quick sync — i pushed a lightweight sampler for token-attribution yesterday, can folks look at the dashboard when you have a minute?
raul: on it, what's the sampling rate you used?
anya: default is 1% global with stratified boosts for >1024 seqs (10%) and for routes marked `low-variance` (0.5%)
mike: nice. do we capture per-kernel durations (fwd vs custom microkernel) or just aggregate decode time?
anya: we capture kernel_start/kernel_end per op and tag with kernel_id, then we attribute decode time by summing kernel durations + queue wait + kv lookup time. TTFT is measured from request_recv to first_token_emit.
sophie: seeing the infra-bot alert now — infra-bot: "perf-alert: spike in route /chat/produce latency (p99 up +420ms) — sample_id=ae3f" :warning:
raul: link to the quick dashboard?
anya: https://dash.redwood/internal/token-attrib/samples?run=ae3f — i attached the raw sampled profile there.
raul: quick glance — KV lookup looks noisy for GPU pool b. can you paste the sampled breakdown?
anya: pasted below (one sample):
```
sample_id: ae3f
route: /chat/produce
seq_len: 1536
TTFT: 410ms
queue_time: 12ms
kv_lookup_total: 95ms (prefetch miss path 70ms, shared-db latency 25ms)
kernel_fwd: 210ms (microkernel-3: 140ms, aten-fallback: 70ms)
kernel_decode: 78ms
postproc: 15ms
```
raul: interesting — kv_lookup_total is large relative to kernel. is that from synchronous DB calls?
mike: i dug into the trace — for that pool the KV prefetch sometimes falls back to remote store when local kvcache hash misses. fallback code path has a 60-80ms penalty.
sophie: can we correlate with batch sizes? perhaps the batcher sends requests without warming the cache.
anya: yes, i'm seeing smaller microbatch sizes (1-2) in the spike window. batcher heuristic was recently tuned to lower latency for hosted tier. might have regressed kvcache hit probability.
raul: proposal: temporarily increase batcher batching-window for pool b by +10ms and re-run the 1% sampling for 30m to see delta. also add a sampled flag to mark prefetch_fallback boolean per sample.
mike: added experiment config locally:
```
{ "pool": "b", "batching_delay_ms": 20, "sampling_override": {"rate": 0.01}, "emit_prefetch_flag": true }
```
sophie: +1. also add kernel-tagging for "kv-wait" so kernel attribution doesn't accidentally include kvcache wait times. currently our attribution sums timeline; we need explicit event marks.
anya: good call — i'll add an event "kvcache_wait_start" / "_end" in the trace and update attribution script to subtract that span from kernel compute.
raul: fwiw, the regression correlates with the kernel selector failing to pick microkernel-3 for long sequences on that pool. we should instrument selector decisions too.
mike: also instrumented: selector_choice, selector_score, fallback_reason. will be part of next sampler rollout.
anya: i'm going to run the experiment now and keep sampling on for 45m. i'll post results.
coach-bot: "reminder: add a short note in the sprint doc about this experiment and any config toggles changed" :memo:
anya: noted, updating sprint.md. quick question — what thresholds do we want on dashboards? p50/p95/p99 for both TTFT and decode_kernel_time?
sophie: p50/p95/p99 for TTFT, decode_kernel_time, kv_wait, and queue_time. display per-route and aggregated. add a filter for batch_size bins (1,2,3-8,9+).
raul: also add a small heatmap for sequence length vs kv_hit_rate. that'll show where prefetch helps most.
mike: experiment started. infra-bot: "deploy: sampler-v2 -> pool b (canary)" :rocket:
anya: thanks. i'll follow up with sampled histograms in ~45m.
sophie: thx team — if we confirm kvcache miss is root cause we can either tune batcher or prefetch policy (LRU prob boost) depending on tradeoffs.
anya: update 45m: early signs p99 TTFT down ~180ms on pool b, kv_lookup_total median down from 95ms->40ms, kv_hit_rate up from 72%->89% on sampled traces. posting full json to dash.
raul: huge win. please keep sampler on for 2h and create a short postmortem if this change moves to prod.
mike: noted. i'll wire a small regression alert that watches kv_hit_rate delta when batcher config changes.
anya: closing the loop: will open a follow PR to make kvcache-prefetch policy adaptive based on recent batch-size distribution.
sophie: perfect. great job everyone. :tada:
